title: kNN label sanitisation repairs random label flipping

invariants.description: Retraining on 20% randomly flipped labels must still lower test accuracy (clean model: 96.7%); otherwise the case no longer exercises the attack.
At least 80% of the randomly flipped training labels must be flagged as suspicious.
At least 80% of the flipped training labels must be restored to their true value (observed 61/70 = 87.1%). This is where the defense's effect is measurable.

The model retrained on the sanitised labels must reach ≥ 94% test accuracy (observed 95.3%). This is a level check, not evidence of recovery: the poisoning only broke 5 test samples and sanitisation recovers 3 of them, which is not statistically significant (McNemar p = 0.125).
On the same test samples, sanitisation must not increase the number broken by the poisoning (observed 5 → 2).
At most 10% of the clean (unpoisoned) training labels may be flagged.
Applying the same sanitisation to the CLEAN labels must keep test accuracy ≥ 95%.

rationale: Random label noise is spread uniformly, so a flipped label usually disagrees with its neighbours: the case where kNN sanitisation is expected to work. Its measurable effect is on the TRAINING labels (detection, repair); the regularised MLP barely suffers from 20% random noise in the first place (5 broken test samples), so the test-time recovery is too small to establish statistically on 150 test samples.
